chapter.title: Broken
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the PowerPyx 100% chart (16 boxes, 15 labels) and the game’s text (the detroitbecometext template resolved against the string table). AFTER PARTY (checkpoint) → ENTER LIVING ROOM → POUR WHISKY → [ CHECK STUDIO WITHOUT CARL | CHECK STUDIO WITH CARL ] → CONFRONT LEO (REASON / ORDER / ADVISE / WARN) → BREAK MIND PALACE → MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT → [ OBEY CARL (button ENDURE) → CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK → POLICE ARRIVE → LEO ACCUSED MARKUS | PUSH LEO → LEO IS HURT → (EXPLAIN / BEG / CONJURE / SAY NOTHING) → POLICE ARRIVE → POLICE MISTOOK MARKUS FOR THE AGGRESSOR ]. Two endings, both cross-chapter impacts; Markus is shot on both. No probability, timer value, relationship, public-opinion or instability change anywhere in the chapter. Cross-chapter: Carl alive or dead (`carl`) decides the Waiting for Hank magazine and the Night of the Soul visit (house or grave); Leo’s fate is `ch08Leo`. Researched in docs/research/ch08-broken.md.

decisions.title: After Party (checkpoint) and Enter Living Room
decisions.context: Carl and Markus come home from a party: “No one gives a damn about art.” Carl wants a drink in the living room.

options.label: Wheel Carl into the living room
Go ahead alone
options.effect: Carl: “Are you planning on drinking alone, Markus?” Markus: “Sorry, Carl... I’m coming.” Nothing changes.

decisions.note: Chart nodes AFTER PARTY (checkpoint) and ENTER LIVING ROOM (unmissable action). Going ahead alone is the template’s conditioned variant “Go without Carl”, not a button prompt.

benchmark.note: An event for the arrival, quoting the template, then a movement choice that only changes Carl’s line. No stat change.

decisions.title: Pour Whisky and call the police
decisions.context: “Scotch, neat, as usual?” Carl: “I’m old enough to choose my own medication… Did you leave the light on in the studio?” He has Markus call the police (the single-button prompt CALL).

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: The police are called; a patrol car is on the way.

decisions.gate: Always, after entering the living room.
decisions.note: Chart node POUR WHISKY (unmissable). The call to the police has no chart node.

benchmark.note: One narrated event quoting the template; the address and Carl’s surname are name tokens.

decisions.title: Check the studio with or without Carl?

options.label: Check studio without Carl
options.effect: Carl: “Markus, no! I wanna come with you!” He is in the studio anyway.

decisions.note: Chart choice group CHECK STUDIO WITHOUT CARL / CHECK STUDIO WITH CARL; both rejoin at CONFRONT LEO and nothing later depends on it.

benchmark.note: A two-option decision in the chart’s order; the outcomes are the template’s two conditioned variants.

decisions.title: Confront Leo: what to say?
decisions.context: Leo is taking Carl’s paintings, “a down payment on my inheritance”. Carl: “Markus, get him away from there. Get him outta here!”

options.label: REASON
options.effect: “Be reasonable... this isn’t going to get you anywhere.”

options.label: ORDER
options.effect: “Leo, don’t make this difficult, listen to your father. You need to leave... Now.”

options.label: ADVISE
options.effect: “Listen, you should go before things get worse.”

options.label: WARN
options.effect: “Look, I’ve already called the Police. You should go now before you get yourself into more trouble.”

decisions.note: Chart node CONFRONT LEO. Every option gets the same reply (“Not perfect like this FUCKING THING?!”); a timeout plays one extra line from Carl.

benchmark.note: The four buttons in the game’s order with the spoken lines; no timeout option (no source gives the timer).

decisions.title: Break Mind Palace and Markus becomes deviant
decisions.context: Carl: “Markus... don’t defend yourself, you hear me?! Don’t do anything.” Leo pushes, slaps and taunts Markus.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Markus breaks his programming on every path.

decisions.note: Chart nodes BREAK MIND PALACE (unmissable button sequence) and MARKUS BECOMES DEVIANT (event). There is no path on which Markus stays obedient.

benchmark.note: One narrated event for both nodes; the button sequence is not modelled, and the inner wall is the benchmark’s rendering.

decisions.title: Endure Leo’s attack or push back?
decisions.context: Leo: “I’m gonna destroy you… YOU’RE NOTHING!” Carl has told Markus not to defend himself; Markus is already deviant.

options.label: Endure (chart: OBEY CARL)
options.effect: Carl falls from his wheelchair and dies of a heart attack.

options.label: Push Leo
options.effect: Leo falls and hits his head on the wheelchair lift (LEO IS HURT); Carl lives.

decisions.note: Police shoot Markus on either route; the later Carl scene changes (Night of the Soul: his house if he lived, his grave if he died; Waiting for Hank: which magazine is on the desk).

benchmark.note: The game’s buttons ENDURE and PUSH LEO in the chart’s order (the template lists PUSH LEO first). Sets `ch08Leo`; Carl’s death (`carl` false) is applied at the next scene.

decisions.title: Carl dies of a heart attack; Leo accused Markus
decisions.context: Carl: “Remember, Markus… Don’t let anybody… Tell you who you are…” Leo: “The android… It was the android!”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Carl dies; the police shoot Markus. Ending LEO ACCUSED MARKUS.

decisions.note: Chart nodes CARL DIES OF A HEART ATTACK, POLICE ARRIVE and the ending LEO ACCUSED MARKUS (cross-chapter impact).

benchmark.note: Two narrated events quoting the template; the first sets `carl` to false, the second records the ending in `ch08Ending`.

decisions.title: Leo is hurt; Markus pleads with Carl; police mistook Markus for the aggressor
decisions.context: Carl, crawling to his son: “They’ll destroy you, Markus! You gotta go! Get outta here!”

options.label: EXPLAIN
options.effect: “Carl… I… I… I didn’t mean to…”

options.label: BEG
options.effect: “Carl, no... No, please, I don’t want to leave you…”

options.label: CONJURE
options.effect: “Go?.. I have nowhere to go... Carl, you’re all I have!”

decisions.note: Chart nodes LEO IS HURT, POLICE ARRIVE and the ending POLICE MISTOOK MARKUS FOR THE AGGRESSOR (cross-chapter impact). The four-button plea is not on the chart and changes nothing: Carl shouts “GET OUT! NOW! GO!” and the police shoot Markus. Leo survives (hospitalized).

benchmark.note: The plea as a decision with the game’s buttons, then a narrated event that records the ending in `ch08Ending`. Carl stays alive.
